body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_+\), exactly one slice \(M_i\) has rank two, and its label is \(a\); the other two slices have rank three. Every nonzero \(\widetilde k\in\ker(M_a)\) has nonzero coordinates, and \(b\) is the unique label whose coordinate has sign opposite to \(\widetilde k_a\). With \(c=\mathcal V\setminus\{a,b\}\), \(N=\operatorname{adj}(M_a)e_c\), and \(W=M_bN\),
\[
v=\frac{W_c}{W_b},\qquad u=-\frac{N_aW_b}{N_bW_b+N_cW_c},\qquad \operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v).
\]
Uniformly on \(\mathcal P_+\),
\[
|W_b|\ge d_W,\qquad |D|\ge d_D,\qquad |\det(M_b)|\ge d_b,\qquad |\det(M_c)|\ge d_c.
\]
Thus \(C_3(P)\) globally identifies the labeled chain and both direct coefficients, and \(\operatorname{Rec}\) has constant arithmetic cost.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_+\) and write its causal order as \(\pi=(a,b,c)\).  By the cubic-factorization lemma,
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M_a)=2,
\qquad
\det(M_b)=hrtu pz^2,
\]
and
\[
\det(M_c)=hrtu v^2qz^2+hrwuvqy^2+htwvqx^2+rtwuv^2.
\]
Every factor in the expression for \(\det(M_b)\) is strictly positive.  Every summand in the expression for \(\det(M_c)\) is strictly positive.  Thus \(M_b\) and \(M_c\) are nonsingular, while \(M_a\) has rank two.  Hence \(a\) is the unique label of a rank-two slice.

The same lemma gives
\[
\ker(M_a)=\operatorname{span}\{k\},
\qquad
k=(-uz,z+vy,-y)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Positivity of \(u,v,y,z\) shows that the signs of the \((a,b,c)\) coordinates of \(k\) are \((-,+,-)\), and none is zero.  Every nonzero \(\widetilde k\in\ker(M_a)\) is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(k\); multiplication by a negative scalar reverses all three signs simultaneously.  Therefore the \(b\)-coordinate is, independently of the chosen representative, the unique coordinate with sign opposite to the \(a\)-coordinate.  This identifies \(b\), and \(c\) is the remaining label.

Put \(K=hxr\).  Direct cofactor expansion of
\(M_a=hxgg^{\mathsf T}+rdd^{\mathsf T}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{adj}(M_a)=Kkk^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Since \(k_c=-y\), the chosen adjugate column is
\[
N=\operatorname{adj}(M_a)e_c
=Kk k_c
=K\begin{pmatrix}uyz\\-y(z+vy)\\y^2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both \(g^{\mathsf T}N\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}N\) vanish, whereas
\[
e^{\mathsf T}N=N_b+vN_c=-Kyz.
\]
Using \(M_b=hpgg^{\mathsf T}+rudd^{\mathsf T}+tee^{\mathsf T}\), it follows equation by equation that
\[
W=M_bN=t e(e^{\mathsf T}N)
=-Ktyz\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\v\end{pmatrix}.
\]
In particular,
\[
W_b=-Ktyz,
\qquad
W_c=-Ktvyz,
\qquad
\frac{W_c}{W_b}=v.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
D=N_bW_b+N_cW_c
=K^2ty^2z(z+vy)-K^2tvy^3z
=K^2ty^2z^2,
\]
and
\[
-N_aW_b=K^2tu y^2z^2.
\]
All factors in \(W_b\) and \(D\) are nonzero, so both divisions are legitimate and
\[
u=-\frac{N_aW_b}{D},
\qquad
v=\frac{W_c}{W_b}.
\]

It remains to verify the asserted uniform margins.  The box restrictions imply
\[
h\ge\frac12,
\qquad
r,t,w\ge\left(\frac34\right)^3\frac12=\frac{27}{128},
\qquad
x,y,z,u,v\ge\frac14,
\]
as well as
\[
p=ux+y\ge\frac{5}{16},
\qquad
q=vp+z\ge\frac{21}{64},
\qquad
K=hxr\ge\frac{27}{1024}.
\]
Therefore
\[
|W_b|=Ktyz
\ge \frac{27}{1024}\frac{27}{128}\frac14\frac14
=\frac{729}{2097152}=d_W,
\]
and
\[
|D|=K^2ty^2z^2
\ge\left(\frac{27}{1024}\right)^2\frac{27}{128}
\left(\frac14\right)^4
=\frac{19683}{34359738368}=d_D.
\]
Likewise,
\[
\det(M_b)=hrtu pz^2
\ge\frac12\left(\frac{27}{128}\right)^2
\frac14\frac{5}{16}\left(\frac14\right)^2
=\frac{3645}{33554432}=d_b.
\]
Keeping only the last positive summand of \(\det(M_c)\) gives
\[
\det(M_c)\ge rtwuv^2
\ge\left(\frac{27}{128}\right)^3\frac14
\left(\frac14\right)^2
=\frac{19683}{134217728}=d_c.
\]

Now suppose the same observed tensor \(C\) arose from a second member of \(\mathcal P_+\).  The unique rank-two slice is intrinsic to \(C\), so the second representation has the same root \(a\).  The kernel sign rule, also intrinsic to \(C\), then gives the same middle \(b\), hence the same terminal \(c\).  Finally, \(N,W,D\) are functions only of \(C\) and these recovered labels, and the proved denominator bounds make the two displayed ratios well defined; the two representations must consequently have the same \(u\) and \(v\).  Thus the structural target is uniquely determined by the observed cubic tensor, rather than defined to equal an observable functional, and the definition of \(\operatorname{Rec}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v).
\]
The recovery evaluates three fixed-size determinants, one \(3\times3\) adjugate, finitely many sign comparisons, and two scalar ratios.  Since \(|\mathcal V|=3\), this is constant arithmetic cost in the real-arithmetic model.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: skewness alone recovers the unknown mechanism globally rather than selecting among algebraic candidates.
body.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, reports nonidentification through order three on the fixed unrestricted graph; Cai et al. (2023) does not recover this unknown six-chain structure from \(C_3\) alone.
body.consumer: CEId-from-Moments can replace its fourth-cumulant one-proxy initializer by a certified cubic branch on the positive-skew chamber.
